meta.task: T24 energy kill test parameter sheet
meta.conventions: nominal/optimistic follow the frozen selection rules; derived numbers are marked 'derived'; unit conversions: eta = R x 1.24/1.55; J/MAC = 2/(TOPS/W) x 1e-12; heater mean power = P_2pi/2; modulator energy per symbol = per bit for NRZ. Gathering was done by the lead agent plus three delegated sub-agents (PD/TIA, lasers/TEC, digital INT8); the lead re-opened and re-checked: Horowitz table image, Tan/Ceccarelli/Flamini/Pentangelo/Skryabin texts, converter surveys, modulator papers, Excelitas row, Semtech GN1052WA2 page, Micromachines TIA quote, Liu 2025 Ge PD abstract, G&H and Thorlabs datasheet lines and plots, Garrod/Liu/Hsu/Intel/TSMC abstracts. Items read only by a sub-agent are tagged in the notes.

nominal_source.title: 10.2 A Single-Channel 2.6GS/s 10b Dynamic Pipelined ADC with Time-Assisted Residue Generation Scheme Achieving Intrinsic PVT Robustness (Hao et al., ISSCC 2023)
nominal_source.where: ISSCC 2023 paper 10.2; power, fs and SNDR as tabulated in Murmann ADC survey rev20260801 (sheet ISSCC) and in the ISSCC program abstract
nominal_source.quote: this ADC achieves 51.4dB SNDR with 13.9mW power consumption
nominal_source.conditions: 28 nm CMOS, 0.9 V, single channel, fs = 2.6 GS/s, P = 13.9 mW, SNDR(hf) 51.4 dB at fin = 1.3 GHz, ENOB = 8.25. Method: energy per sample = reported power / sample rate = 13.9 mW / 2.6 GS/s = 5.346 pJ. Chosen because it is the median design of the 15 ISSCC/VLSI ADCs 2018-2026 with 1-10 GS/s and ENOB 7-9 in the survey (median P/fs = 5.35 pJ; quartiles 2.55 / 5.35 / 7.63 pJ). Walden alternative: FoMW 17.6 fJ/conv-step x 2^8 = 4.51 pJ.

optimistic_source.title: A 3-mW 2.7-GS/s 8b Subranging ADC with Multiple-Reference-Embedded Comparators (Wang and Kuo, ISSCC 2023, paper 17.7)
optimistic_source.where: ISSCC 2023 paper 17.7 abstract (as logged in the Murmann ADC survey, ISSCC sheet)
optimistic_source.quote: It achieves 45.9dB SNDR in 3mW resulting in a 6.9fJ/conv.-step Walden FoM.
optimistic_source.conditions: 28 nm CMOS, 1 V, 8b subranging, fs = 2.7 GS/s, P = 3.0 mW, SNDR 45.9 dB at fin = 1.25 GHz (ENOB 7.33). Method: reported power / sample rate = 3.0 mW / 2.7 GS/s = 1.111 pJ. Lowest P/fs of all 15 survey designs in the 1-10 GS/s, ENOB 7-9 window. Walden-normalised to 8 bit: 6.895 fJ/conv-step x 256 = 1.77 pJ (use this if ENOB < 8 matters).

adc_energy_j.notes: Method stated: P/fs (reported power / sample rate) for both values; the 8-bit Walden-normalised equivalents are 4.51 pJ (nominal) and 1.77 pJ (optimistic). Survey filter: ISSCC+VLSI sheets, year >= 2018, 1 <= fs <= 10 GS/s, 7 <= ENOB(SNDR_hf) <= 9, n = 15. Commercial parts are far higher: TI ADC12DJ3200 (12-bit, 6.4 GSPS single channel) lists 'Power consumption (typ) (mW) 3000' on ti.com/product/ADC12DJ3200, i.e. about 470 pJ/sample. The survey covers ISSCC and VLSI papers only (peer-reviewed conference papers).

nominal_source.title: 3.4 A 36Gb/s PAM4 transmitter using an 8b 18GS/S DAC in 28nm CMOS (Nazemi et al., ISSCC 2015)
nominal_source.where: Power value from DAC Performance Survey 1996-2020 (Caragiulo, Daigle, Murmann), data.csv row Ref=84 (M=8, Fs=18000 MS/s, Power 84 mW); the ISSCC abstract itself gives only the 8b 18GS/s DAC, not the power
nominal_source.quote: A 36Gb/s PAM4 transmitter using an 8b 18GS/S DAC in 28nm CMOS
nominal_source.conditions: 28 nm CMOS, current-steering, 8 bit, fs = 18 GS/s, P = 84 mW (survey value), supplies 1/1.5 V. Method: reported power / sample rate = 84 mW / 18 GS/s = 4.667 pJ. Chosen as the median of the nine 8-bit entries (fs >= 1 GS/s, 2015-2021) in the survey: 3.08, 3.14, 3.18, 3.57, 4.67, 5.11, 9.33, 14.84, 25.0 pJ.

optimistic_source.title: A 2x Time-Interleaved 28-GS/s 8-Bit 0.03-mm2 Switched-Capacitor DAC in 16-nm FinFET CMOS (Caragiulo, Mattia, Arbabian, Murmann, IEEE JSSC 56, 2335)
optimistic_source.where: abstract (also Chapter 4 of P. Caragiulo, Stanford PhD thesis 2022, purl.stanford.edu/rz812rb9519, power breakdown)
optimistic_source.quote: consuming 88 mW from a single 0.8-V supply
optimistic_source.conditions: 16 nm FinFET, 8 bit, fs = 28 GS/s, P = 88 mW incl. digital MUX 12 mW, SC DAC cores 24 mW, clock RX 14 mW, clock distribution 30 mW, analog MUX+buffer 8 mW (thesis Sec. 4.4); drives 100 ohm differential load, 0.32 Vpp swing, SFDR >= 37 dB, IM3 <= -45.6 dBc. Method: reported power / sample rate = 88 mW / 28 GS/s = 3.143 pJ.

dac_energy_j.notes: No 8-bit DAC in the survey is below about 3.1 pJ/sample (Tan VLSI 2018 3.08 pJ at 112 GS/s is a 112-GS/s SST DAC-TX, 345 mW). Same-group 14 GS/s 8-bit DAC: 50 mW -> 3.57 pJ (VLSI 2020, DOI 10.1109/VLSICircuits18222.2020.9162776, abstract: 'consuming 50 mW from a single 0.8 V supply'). IBM 72-GS/s 8-bit DAC-based TX in 4 nm: 288 mW -> 4.0 pJ (JSSC 58, 1074, DOI 10.1109/JSSC.2022.3228632, abstract 'The TX consumes 288 mW from a 0.95-V power supply'). These are research converters at 14-100 GS/s; no 8-bit DAC in the 1-10 GS/s window was found in the survey. Commercial DACs are far higher: TI DAC38RF86 (14-bit, 9 GSPS) lists 'Power Dissipation: 1.4 to 2.2 W/ch' on ti.com/product/DAC38RF86, i.e. 156-244 pJ/sample per channel.

modulator_energy_j.unit: J per symbol (NRZ/OOK, 1 bit = 1 symbol), driver INCLUDED, laser excluded

nominal_source.title: 8-lambda x 50 Gbps/lambda Heterogeneously Integrated Si-Ph DWDM Transmitter (Levy et al., IEEE JSSC 59, 690)
nominal_source.quote: energy efficiency at 50 Gb/s of the high-speed electronics, including serializer overhead, is 1.17 pJ/bit
nominal_source.conditions: Silicon microring modulators + 28 nm CMOS drivers (2 Vpp), NRZ 50 Gb/s per wavelength, driver INCLUDED (also includes serializer overhead); laser excluded; ring thermal tuning not in this figure (Kawahara et al. Table 1 lists the same transmitter as 1.3 pJ/bit with driver + MRM + tuning). 1 symbol = 1 bit (NRZ).

optimistic_source.title: A 40Gb/s Optical NRZ Transmitter Based on Monolithic Microring Modulators in 45nm SOI CMOS (Lin, Moazeni, Stojanovic, VLSI Circuits 2018)
optimistic_source.quote: It achieves 330fJ/b complete transmitter energy (including clock distribution and serializer sub-systems)
optimistic_source.conditions: Monolithic 45 nm SOI CMOS microring modulator, NRZ 40 Gb/s, differential driver + AC coupler INCLUDED, also includes clock distribution and serializer; 3 dB extinction ratio and 4.7 dB insertion loss at 40 Gb/s; ring thermal tuning not stated in the figure. 1 symbol = 1 bit (NRZ).

modulator_energy_j.notes: Driver included in both values. Best Si Mach-Zehnder driver+modulator results: 0.70 pJ/bit at 112 GBd NRZ (78 mW; Li et al., Nature Electronics 6, 910 (2023), DOI 10.1038/s41928-023-01048-1, number read in the Research Square preprint Table 1, DOI 10.21203/rs.3.rs-1980286/v1, and quoted in Kawahara et al. Table 1; abstract of the published paper says 'energy efficiencies below picojoules per bit') and 0.78 pJ/bit at 64 GBd NRZ (50 mW incl. 5-tap Rx FFE; Kawahara et al., IEEE JSTQE 32 (2026), DOI 10.1109/JSTQE.2025.3640645, abstract). Rows of Kawahara Table 1 (driver + modulator, Si, NRZ unless noted): 0.7, 0.78, 0.88, 1.3, 1.5 (SiGe EAM, PAM4), 5.35, 5.5 (PAM4), 11.4, 22 pJ/bit. THIN-FILM LiNbO3: NO peer-reviewed TFLN modulator-plus-driver energy per symbol was found; modulator-only (driverless) TFLN: 4.49 fJ/bit at 100 GBd PAM4 (Optics Express 30, 25308 (2022), DOI 10.1364/OE.458431, abstract 'power consumption of 4.49fj/bit', V_pi 0.7 V, driver excluded); TFLN IQ modulator estimated 120 fJ/bit (Xu et al., Nat. Commun. 11, 3911, DOI 10.1038/s41467-020-17806-0, computed from V_rms; driver excluded). The TFLN numbers exclude the 2-4 Vpp-class driver that dominates real transmitters, so they are NOT used for nominal/optimistic. For multi-level (analog) drive a linear driver is needed and the per-symbol energy is higher than NRZ values; PAM4 per-symbol = 2x the per-bit values quoted by the cited papers.

nominal_source.title: Femtosecond laser writing low-loss waveguides in silica glass: highly symmetrical mode field and mechanism of refractive index change (Tan, Sun, Qiu, Opt. Mater. Express 11, 848)
nominal_source.where: abstract (Crossref); wavelength 1550 nm is stated by the secondary source Skryabin et al. arXiv:2408.06688 Introduction ('optimized to 0.15 dB/cm at the wavelength of 1550 nm [58, 59]'); full text of the OME paper could not be opened (publisher bot wall)
nominal_source.quote: The waveguides exhibit a low propagation loss of 0.15 dB/cm and a symmetrical mode field.
nominal_source.conditions: single-mode waveguides in silica glass, fs laser; measurement wavelength not stated in the abstract (1550 nm per Skryabin et al.). Borosilicate (EAGLE XG) alternative at 1550 nm: 0.29 dB/cm (Ceccarelli et al. 2020, Laser Photonics Rev. 14, 2000024) and ~0.6 dB/cm (Flamini et al. 2015).

optimistic_source.title: Effectively writing low propagation and bend loss waveguides in the silica glass by using a femtosecond laser (Tan, Sun, Li, Qiu, Opt. Lett. 47, 4766)
optimistic_source.quote: A record low propagation loss of 0.07 dB/cm is achieved
optimistic_source.conditions: silica glass, fs laser, writing speed 125 um/s, bend loss 0.001 dB/mm at 30 mm radius. The abstract does not state the wavelength; Skryabin et al. (arXiv:2408.06688, Introduction) cite it as 'a record low PL of 0.07 dB/cm has been demonstrated at 1550 nm with a total chip IL of 1.07 dB [60]' (ref. [60] = this paper). Full text not opened (paywall / bot wall).

fs_propagation_loss_db_per_cm.notes: CHECK RESULT: the project's 0.07 dB/cm for Tan et al. OL 47, 4766 is correct as the abstract value (DOI 10.1364/OL.470670 resolves; title/volume/page verified via Crossref) but the 1550-nm wavelength is confirmed only through the Skryabin et al. citation. Not to be confused with Skryabin et al. 2024 (Phys. Rev. Applied; arXiv:2408.06688), who also report 0.07 dB/cm but measured at 920 nm.

fs_coupling_loss_db_per_facet.unit: dB per facet, fiber (SMF-28) to fs-written waveguide at 1550 nm

nominal_source.title: Low power reconfigurability and reduced crosstalk in integrated photonic circuits fabricated by femtosecond laser micromachining (Ceccarelli et al., Laser Photonics Rev. 14, 2000024)
nominal_source.where: Section 2 (Device structure) and Discussion (coupling losses 'only 0.54 dB' for two facets)
nominal_source.quote: with losses as low as 0.27 dB/facet
nominal_source.conditions: Corning EAGLE XG boro-aluminosilicate, waveguides optimized for 1550 nm, mode diameter 9 um (1/e^2), propagation loss 0.29 dB/cm. 'as low as' indicates a best case for this platform.

optimistic_source.title: Thermally reconfigurable quantum photonic circuits at telecom wavelength by femtosecond laser micromachining (Flamini et al., Light Sci. Appl. 4, e354)
optimistic_source.quote: coupling losses to standard single-mode telecom fibers of 0.2 dB per facet
optimistic_source.conditions: borosilicate glass, 1550 nm, mode diameter about 13.5 um; the 0.2 dB is retrieved from the overlap integral of measured mode profiles (calculated mode-matching loss, not a measured insertion loss).

fs_coupling_loss_db_per_facet.notes: Skryabin et al. 2024 (arXiv:2408.06688) measure 0.2 dB/facet on average in fused silica (mode overlap > 98.8%) but at 920 nm, so it is NOT used for 1550 nm. Pentangelo et al. (Nanophotonics 13, 2259 (2024), DOI 10.1515/nanoph-2023-0636, arXiv:2310.19718) report total insertion loss of 2.5 dB at 1550 nm for a 6-mode, 90-mm-long, 15-MZI processor including both fiber couplings; realistic fiber-array chips with long fan-in/out will not reach the best-case facet loss.

loss_per_stage_db.unit: dB per MZI stage (ALL-INCLUSIVE on-chip loss of one interferometer incl. its propagation length), 1550 nm, fs-written

nominal_source.title: Low power reconfigurability and reduced crosstalk in integrated photonic circuits fabricated by femtosecond laser micromachining (Ceccarelli et al., Laser Photonics Rev. 14, 2000024)
nominal_source.where: Discussion (comparison with silicon PIC of Harris et al.)
nominal_source.conditions: 1550 nm, EAGLE XG; MZI = two 3 dB directional couplers (1.2 mm interaction length, 9 um spacing) + S-bends (radius 45 mm) + 3 mm arms, propagation loss 0.29 dB/cm; the 0.35 dB is the on-chip total per interferometer, i.e. it INCLUDES waveguide propagation along the MZI. Text: 'Our technology shows comparable results in terms of on-chip losses (about 0.35 dB/interferometer)'.

optimistic_source.title: Low power reconfigurability and reduced crosstalk in integrated photonic circuits fabricated by femtosecond laser micromachining (Ceccarelli et al., Laser Photonics Rev. 14, 2000024)
optimistic_source.conditions: No better measured per-MZI value at 1550 nm in fs-written glass was found, so optimistic = nominal.

loss_per_stage_db.notes: AVOID DOUBLE COUNTING: the 0.35 dB already contains the propagation loss of the MZI footprint; no source isolating the pure directional-coupler excess loss at 1550 nm was opened. Cross-check (derived, assumptions flagged): Pentangelo et al. 2024 (DOI 10.1515/nanoph-2023-0636) UPP B at 1550 nm: total IL 2.5 dB, 15 MZIs in a 6-mode rectangular mesh (cell length 13.2 mm, chip 90 mm); if the light crosses up to 6 stages and 2 facets cost 2 x 0.27 dB, the per-stage on-chip loss is <= (2.5 - 0.54)/6 = 0.33 dB. Quote: 'insertion losses at 785 nm (1550 nm) lower than 3 dB (2.5 dB)'. Silicon PIC reference in the same paper: 0.1 dB/interferometer.

modulator_insertion_loss_db.unit: dB on-chip insertion loss of a TFLN Mach-Zehnder-type modulator, fiber coupling excluded

nominal_source.title: High-performance coherent optical modulators based on thin-film lithium niobate platform (Xu et al., Nat. Commun. 11, 3911)
nominal_source.where: Results (optical loss), arXiv text: fibre-to-fibre 8.6 dB and 8.25 dB, grating couplers 3.4 dB/facet -> on-chip 1.8 dB and 1.45 dB for the 13 mm and 7.5 mm devices
nominal_source.quote: the on-chip losses are 1.8 dB and 1.45 dB for 13mm and 7.5mm device
nominal_source.conditions: TFLN IQ (nested Mach-Zehnder) modulators, 1550 nm; nominal = midpoint of the two reported device lengths ((1.8 + 1.45)/2 = 1.625 dB).

optimistic_source.title: Breaking voltage-bandwidth limits in integrated lithium niobate modulators using micro-structured electrodes (Kharel et al., Optica 8, 357)
optimistic_source.quote: we maintain a on-chip loss of < 1 dB
optimistic_source.conditions: HyperLight TFLN MZM, 1550 nm, 20 mm electrode, V_pi 1.3 V; the value is an upper bound ('< 1 dB'); an Optica erratum exists (DOI 10.1364/OPTICA.440484) and the corrected text was not opened.

modulator_insertion_loss_db.notes: Other points: hybrid Si-LiNbO3 MZM insertion loss 2.5 dB (He et al., Nature Photonics 13, 359 (2019), DOI 10.1038/s41566-019-0378-6, arXiv:1807.10362 abstract: 'insertion loss of 2.5 dB'); silicon microring modulator in the 330 fJ/b transmitter above: 4.7 dB insertion loss at 40 Gb/s (VLSI 2018 abstract). A lower TFLN on-chip loss than 1 dB may exist (e.g. Wang et al. Nature 562, 101 (2018)) but could not be verified here (abstract not available).

heater_mean_power_w.unit: W mean electrical power per thermo-optic phase shifter for a phase uniformly distributed in [0, 2pi) = P_2pi / 2; 1550 nm, fs-written borosilicate with thermal isolation

nominal_source.title: High-fidelity and polarization-insensitive universal photonic processors fabricated by femtosecond laser writing (Pentangelo et al., Nanophotonics 13, 2259)
nominal_source.where: Section III (calibration) and abstract/introduction: average 2pi power per phase shifter
nominal_source.quote: 39 mW for UPP A and 63 mW for UPP B
nominal_source.conditions: UPP B = 6-mode, 15-MZI, 30-heater processor at 1550 nm, EAGLE XG, gold microheaters with 300 um deep, 60 um wide, 3 mm long isolation trenches; P_2pi = 63 mW average over the 30 shifters; mean for uniform phase = 63/2 = 31.5 mW. (UPP A at 785 nm: 39 mW.) Phase-power relation is quadratic-in-voltage / linear in power, so mean over [0, 2pi) = P_2pi/2.

optimistic_source.title: Low power reconfigurability and reduced crosstalk in integrated photonic circuits fabricated by femtosecond laser micromachining (Ceccarelli et al., Laser Photonics Rev. 14, 2000024)
optimistic_source.quote: with a power dissipation as low as 0.72 mW
optimistic_source.conditions: 1550 nm, EAGLE XG, bridge waveguide (ablated under the MZI arm) operated in HIGH VACUUM: P_2pi = 0.72 mW -> mean 0.36 mW; switching time ~960 ms. THIS REQUIRES A VACUUM PACKAGE. In ambient air the same bridge needs P_2pi = 37 mW -> mean 18.5 mW; with 450 um deep trenches only: 57 mW -> 28.5 mW; with no isolation: 611 mW -> 305.5 mW.

heater_mean_power_w.notes: Optimistic follows the frozen rule literally (best demonstrated, vacuum). If the requester prefers an air-ambient optimistic value use P_2pi = 37 mW (Ceccarelli 2020, 'a complete reconfiguration is achieved with a power dissipation as low as 37 mW') -> mean 0.0185 W. Medium-vacuum point: P_2pi = 1.04 mW (0.52 mW mean). Older/other points: 204 mW per 2pi at 785 nm without trenches (Ceccarelli et al., J. Lightwave Technol. 37, 4275 (2019), DOI 10.1109/JLT.2019.2923126, text 'P2pi = 204 mW'); 38 mW per 2pi with curved trenches at 940 nm (Albiero et al., Micromachines 13, 1145, DOI 10.3390/mi13071145); about 17 mW per 2pi for FLICE-suspended microbridges in borosilicate (Lichtenegger et al., Photonics 13, 731 (2026), DOI 10.3390/photonics13080731, abstract only; wavelength not verified, full text blocked); Flamini 2015 (no isolation, 1550 nm): 0.5 W per 2pi. Total on-chip dissipation of UPP B for random unitaries: 'always lower than 1.9 W'.

quantum_efficiency.unit: external quantum efficiency at 1550 nm (eta = R x 1.24/1.55 = 0.8 R)

nominal_source.title: High Speed InGaAs PIN Photodiodes C30617, C30618 datasheet (Excelitas), Rev. 2016.11.08
nominal_source.where: datasheet p.3, 'Electro-Optical Characteristics (C30617, C30618)': Responsivity at 1550 nm, TO-18 ceramic, min 0.85 / typ 0.95 A/W; Bandwidth (-3dB, RL = 50 ohm) 3.5 GHz
nominal_source.conditions: C30617: 100 um diameter InGaAs PIN, TA = 22 C, VR = 5 V, bare TO-18 (external QE without fibre-coupling loss), 3.5 GHz bandwidth. R(typ) = 0.95 A/W -> eta = 0.95 x 1.24/1.55 = 0.760. Fibre-receptacle version (multimode fibre coupled): 0.70 min / 0.80 typ A/W -> eta = 0.64.

optimistic_source.title: Near-infrared germanium PIN-photodiodes with >1A/W responsivity (Liu et al., Light Sci. Appl. 14, 9)
optimistic_source.quote: at 1.55 µm, this corresponds to a responsivity of 1.15 A/W
optimistic_source.conditions: nanostructured Ge PIN photodiode, zero bias, room temperature, verified EQE above 90% over 1.2-1.6 um (abstract); R = 1.15 A/W -> eta = 1.15 x 1.24/1.55 = 0.92. Large-area free-space device (5 mm diameter per sub-agent reading of the paper), NOT a GHz-class detector.

quantum_efficiency.notes: If the optimistic value must be a high-speed detector: Ge-on-Si waveguide PD, responsivity 1.09 A/W at 1550 nm (eta 0.87), 42.5 GHz at 2 V reverse bias (Fard et al., Opt. Express 24, 27738 (2016), DOI 10.1364/OE.24.027738; abstract only was readable; whether fibre-to-chip coupling loss is excluded is unverified). Other high-speed points: Ge WPD > 1.0 A/W at -1 V, 20-27 GHz (Chen et al., J. Lightwave Technol. 33, 820 (2015), DOI 10.1109/JLT.2014.2367134); InGaAs/InP UTC-PD EQE 86% (Chin. Phys. B 24, 108506 (2015), DOI 10.1088/1674-1056/24/10/108506); Hamamatsu G12180 series typ 1.1 A/W (cutoff only ~0.6 GHz for the 0.3 mm type). Fibre-pigtailed 50 GHz Coherent XPDV21x0R: 0.5-0.65 A/W (eta ~0.52).

current_noise_a_rthz.unit: A/sqrt(Hz) (input-referred current noise density; nominal = 10 pA/sqrt(Hz), optimistic = 2 pA/sqrt(Hz))

nominal_source.title: GN1052WA2 SiGe BiCMOS transimpedance amplifier, product page (Semtech)
nominal_source.where: product page, Features list (page retrieved by the lead on 2026-10-13, 'year' = retrieval/copyright year of the current product page; the datasheet PDF is login-gated and its own date/revision, and the vintage of this long-lived part, are unknown)
nominal_source.conditions: single +3.3 V supply, 180 mW typ, transimpedance 4 kohm into 100 ohm differential load, upper -3 dB bandwidth 13 GHz, 'input noise current = 1 uA rms with a 0.2 pF detector and 1 nH bond wire' (derived flat density 1 uA/sqrt(13 GHz) = 8.8 pA/sqrt(Hz)). Page does not say whether 10 pA/sqrt(Hz) is a spot or band-average value.

optimistic_source.title: A Low-Noise Hybrid-Integrated Balanced Homodyne Receiver with 2.5 GHz Bandwidth and 15 dB Quantum Shot Noise Clearance (Yang et al., Micromachines 16, 1416)
optimistic_source.where: Section on TIA characterization (Figs. 11-13, Table 2), open access; abstract also states 'an input-referred noise current of only 2 pA/sqrt(Hz)'
optimistic_source.quote: The average input-referred noise current of the proposed TIA is approximately 2 pA/√Hz.
optimistic_source.conditions: 180 nm CMOS TIA, 2.5 GHz -3 dB bandwidth, measured average over 0-4 GHz from the output noise PSD divided by sqrt(RBW) and by the gain (98 dBohm, RF = 80 kohm), 300 fF input capacitance, 70 mW at 2 V; integrated noise 104.5 nA rms (104.5 nA/sqrt(2.5 GHz) = 2.09 pA/sqrt(Hz)). Same group, circuit letter: IEEE Solid-State Circuits Lett. 8, 189 (2025), DOI 10.1109/LSSC.2025.3584266 ('A 2 pA/sqrt(Hz) Input-Referred Noise TIA in 180-nm CMOS With 2.5 GHz Bandwidth').

current_noise_a_rthz.notes: Caveat: the very high transimpedance (80 kohm) is what makes the density low; the feedback-resistor thermal limit is sqrt(4kT/R) = 0.45 pA/sqrt(Hz). For a 10 GHz-class receiver the 2 pA/sqrt(Hz) value is optimistic; 10 GHz-class optimistic candidate: InP DHBT TIA DC-10 GHz, 3 pA/sqrt(Hz) measured (Shivan et al., MIKON 2022, DOI 10.23919/MIKON54314.2022.9924881; abstract only, average-vs-spot unverified). Other commercial points (derived from rms specs, flat-noise assumption): Semtech selector guide 2021 GN1069 8.0, GN7069 9.0, GN1068 10.9 pA/sqrt(Hz); Hittite/ADI HMC690 (obsolete, v04.0709) 'Noise Density @ 1 GHz 11.2 (typ)' and '@ 5 GHz 13.4 (typ)' pA/sqrt(Hz); Maxim PHY1090 1100 nA rms max over 7.5 GHz -> 12.7 pA/sqrt(Hz) max. Simulation-only claims (0.9-2 pA/sqrt(Hz)) were excluded.

laser_wall_plug_efficiency.unit: electrical-to-optical efficiency of the laser diode (fraction); nominal EXCLUDES TEC and driver electronics

nominal_source.title: High Power DFB Lasers LM-1530-1570-100 / -080, datasheet DS-7076 Rev 1 (Gooch & Housego)
nominal_source.where: datasheet p.2 electrical table (Iop typ 375 mA, VF max 3 V) and p.3 plots (80 mW unit: output power and voltage vs current); WPE DERIVED by the lead from the plots
nominal_source.quote: Laser drive current Iop 80-100 mW models 375 500 mA
nominal_source.conditions: 14-pin butterfly DFB with internal isolator and PM fibre, Tcase = 25 C, CW. At Iop = 375 mA the plots give about 75 mW ex-fibre at about 2.0 V -> WPE = 75 mW/(0.375 A x 2.0 V) = 10 % (plot-read, +/-10 %). Including the TEC at this point (about 0.05 W, plot-read) gives about 9 %. Thorlabs DFB1550LP (24 mW) is ~17 % and the QPC 500 mW butterfly module <= 4.8 % on the same derivation.

optimistic_source.title: 50% continuous-wave wallplug efficiency from 1.53 um-emitting broad-area diode lasers (Garrod et al., Appl. Phys. Lett. 105, 071101)
optimistic_source.quote: a maximum CW WPE value of 50% is achieved at room temperature
optimistic_source.conditions: InP-based single-quantum-well broad-area chip, 100 um aperture (multimode), ~1 W output, conductively cooled, 1.53 um; chip-level (no TEC, no driver). Outside the 2015-2026 window by one year; multimode, so not directly usable for a single-mode waveguide layer.

laser_wall_plug_efficiency.notes: Single-mode alternatives for optimistic: 28.49 % PCE at 61.54 mW, 1.55 um DFB, room temperature (Liu et al., Opt. Lett. 50, 3018 (2025), DOI 10.1364/OL.561530, abstract); ISLC 2024 monolithic DFB tapered laser 'peak efficiencies over 30%' (Labrecque et al., DOI 10.1109/ISLC57752.2024.10717351, abstract as read by a sub-agent); SPIE 2024 broad-area 1550 nm laser 'maximum wall plug efficiency of 40%' (Kanold et al., DOI 10.1117/12.3001390). Whole-module efficiency including TEC and driver is far lower: RIO ORION 1550 nm module 0.25-0.5 % (datasheet power dissipation 4-6 W for 10-20 mW out; sub-agent reading). Kawahara et al. (JSTQE 2026) assume 20 % wall-plug efficiency for the laser (an assumption, not a measurement).

available_laser_optical_w.unit: W optical, CW, 1550 nm. nominal = single-frequency DFB butterfly ex-fibre; optimistic = highest chip-level CW power (MULTIMODE broad-area)

nominal_source.title: High Power DFB Lasers LM-1530-1570-100 / -080, datasheet DS-7076 Rev 1 (Gooch & Housego)
nominal_source.where: datasheet p.1 (features): 80 mW and 100 mW ex-fibre models; nominal = midpoint 90 mW
nominal_source.conditions: single-frequency DFB, 14-pin butterfly, PM250 fibre, Tcase = 25 C, CW. Entry-level alternative: Thorlabs DFB1550LP 20 mW min (DOC-102831 Rev A, mirror copy); QPC BrightLock 7115-0000 (DFB + semiconductor amplifier, no EDFA) > 500 mW from PM fibre.

optimistic_source.title: 1550 nm broad area large optical cavity laser with 4.9 W CW output power (Kanold et al., Proc. SPIE 12867, High-Power Diode Laser Technology XXII)
optimistic_source.where: title (DOI resolves; abstract details as read by a sub-agent: 100 um stripe, 20 C operation)
optimistic_source.quote: 1550 nm broad area large optical cavity laser with 4.9 W CW output power
optimistic_source.conditions: chip-level, broad-area MULTIMODE InGaAsP MQW laser, CW, no EDFA, no fibre coupling. NOT single-mode.

available_laser_optical_w.notes: W-class SINGLE-MODE semiconductor power also exists without an EDFA: >3.0 W near-diffraction-limited (M2 ~1.2) tapered amplifier, seeded (Leisher et al., SPIE 12119 (2022), DOI 10.1117/12.2611181, title); 2.7 W CW tapered amplifier (Campbell et al., ISLC 2021, DOI 10.1109/ISLC51662.2021.9615754); >2 W single spatial/spectral mode from a monolithic DFB-tapered laser (Labrecque et al., ISLC 2024, DOI 10.1109/ISLC57752.2024.10717351). For a single-mode waveguide layer use 2-3 W as the realistic upper bound; 4.9 W is the literal highest CW 1550 nm semiconductor power found. Vendor-only claims (10-20 W modules) were not verified.

static_power_w.unit: W electrical power of a thermoelectric cooler stabilising a small photonic module

nominal_source.title: Packaging Design and Characterization of a 16-Channel Silicon Photonic Transmitter Module for a 1.6 Tb/s-Class Optical Engine (Hsu et al., Microelectronics 2, 14)
nominal_source.quote: The measured module-level TEC power was 1.2 W.
nominal_source.conditions: measured module-level TEC power of a packaged 16-channel imec silicon-photonic transmitter module (PAM4 drivers and MZM heaters inside the module, fibre arrays, 1310 nm); the TEC also removes driver/heater heat, so this is an upper-end 'module' value rather than a passive-chip value. Set-point/ambient not stated in the abstract.

optimistic_source.title: DFB1550LP 1550 nm, 20 mW DFB butterfly laser datasheet DOC-102831 Rev A (Thorlabs), 14 Jul 2025 (mirror copy)
optimistic_source.where: datasheet p.1, 'TEC Operation (Typical / Max @ TCASE = 25 C / 75 C)': TEC current 0.06 A typ, TEC voltage 0.20 V typ -> 0.012 W (derived I x V)
optimistic_source.conditions: typical TEC electrical power at Tcase = 25 C with the chip setpoint near ambient (almost no heat lift); the same datasheet's maximum (75 C case) is 2.0 A x 4.0 V = 8 W. Gooch & Housego DS-7076: typ 0.1 A x 0.1 V = 0.010 W at Tamb = 25 C, max 4 A x 4 V = 16 W at 70 C.

static_power_w.notes: The 0.012 W value only holds when ambient equals the chip set-point; it is a best case, not a measured stabilisation power for a passive chip. Mid/high points: Marlow NL1011T single-stage TEC Qmax 1.0 W, Imax 1.0 A, Vmax 2.0 V (max 2 W electrical; sub-agent reading); QPC 7115-0000 butterfly typ 3 V x 2.2 A = 6.6 W; RIO ORION module 4 W at 50 C case (whole module incl. driver); AeroDIODE 1550LD-3 TEC max 1 A x 1.5 V = 1.5 W. Hsu et al. also give 3.95 pJ/bit for the transmitter electronics excluding lasers and TEC, 7.83 pJ/bit including laser and TEC (1.6 Tb/s denominator). No peer-reviewed TEC power for a purely passive (non-dissipating) chip was found.

mzi_excess_loss_db.unit: dB per MZI stage (ALL-INCLUSIVE on-chip loss of one interferometer incl. its propagation length), 1550 nm, fs-written

nominal_source.title: Low power reconfigurability and reduced crosstalk in integrated photonic circuits fabricated by femtosecond laser micromachining (Ceccarelli et al., Laser Photonics Rev. 14, 2000024)
nominal_source.where: Discussion (comparison with silicon PIC of Harris et al.)
nominal_source.conditions: 1550 nm, EAGLE XG; MZI = two 3 dB directional couplers (1.2 mm interaction length, 9 um spacing) + S-bends (radius 45 mm) + 3 mm arms, propagation loss 0.29 dB/cm; the 0.35 dB is the on-chip total per interferometer, i.e. it INCLUDES waveguide propagation along the MZI. Text: 'Our technology shows comparable results in terms of on-chip losses (about 0.35 dB/interferometer)'.

optimistic_source.title: Low power reconfigurability and reduced crosstalk in integrated photonic circuits fabricated by femtosecond laser micromachining (Ceccarelli et al., Laser Photonics Rev. 14, 2000024)
optimistic_source.conditions: No better measured per-MZI value at 1550 nm in fs-written glass was found, so optimistic = nominal.

mzi_excess_loss_db.notes: ALIAS of loss_per_stage_db (identical values and sources). AVOID DOUBLE COUNTING: the 0.35 dB already contains the propagation loss of the MZI footprint; no source isolating the pure directional-coupler excess loss at 1550 nm was opened. Cross-check (derived, assumptions flagged): Pentangelo et al. 2024 (DOI 10.1515/nanoph-2023-0636) UPP B at 1550 nm: total IL 2.5 dB, 15 MZIs in a 6-mode rectangular mesh (cell length 13.2 mm, chip 90 mm); if the light crosses up to 6 stages and 2 facets cost 2 x 0.27 dB, the per-stage on-chip loss is <= (2.5 - 0.54)/6 = 0.33 dB. Quote: 'insertion losses at 785 nm (1550 nm) lower than 3 dB (2.5 dB)'. Silicon PIC reference in the same paper: 0.1 dB/interferometer.

fixed_loss_db.unit: dB, COMPUTED = 2 x fs_coupling_loss_db_per_facet + modulator_insertion_loss_db (propagation and per-stage losses NOT included)

nominal_source.title: computed from fs_coupling_loss_db_per_facet (nominal) and modulator_insertion_loss_db (nominal)
nominal_source.where: arithmetic on the two parameters above
nominal_source.conditions: two fibre-chip facets of the fs-written chip; modulator on-chip loss only (no fibre coupling of the modulator chip, none for the photodetector)

optimistic_source.title: computed from fs_coupling_loss_db_per_facet (optimistic) and modulator_insertion_loss_db (optimistic)
optimistic_source.where: arithmetic on the two parameters above
optimistic_source.conditions: same formula with the optimistic values (modulator loss is an upper bound '< 1 dB')

fixed_loss_db.notes: Formula and facet count are assumptions made by the researcher (input and output facet of the fs-written chip + one modulator); change the facet count if the optical layer is fibre-coupled differently. The final energy budget was not computed.

old.title: 1.1 Computing's energy problem (and what we can do about it) (Horowitz, ISSCC 2014)
old.url: https://www.gwern.net/doc/cs/hardware/2014-horowitz-2.pdf (copy of the IEEE paper; table read by rendering page 14, Figure 1.1.9)
old.where: Figure 1.1.9, page 14 of the ISSCC 2014 digest (table: Integer Add 8 bit 0.03pJ, 32 bit 0.1pJ; Mult 8 bit 0.2pJ, 32 bit 3.1pJ)
old.quote: Rough energy costs for various operations in 45nm 0.9V.
old.conditions: 45 nm, 0.9 V. 8-bit integer multiply 0.2 pJ + 8-bit integer add 0.03 pJ = 0.23 pJ/MAC = 2.3e-13 J. Table values CONFIRMED by viewing the figure image (text layer of the PDF is garbled): Integer Add 8 bit 0.03pJ / 32 bit 0.1pJ; Mult 8 bit 0.2pJ / 32 bit 3.1pJ; FP FAdd 16 bit 0.4pJ / 32 bit 0.9pJ; FMult 16 bit 1.1pJ / 32 bit 3.7pJ. These are 'rough' arithmetic-only costs (no data movement).

modern.node: TSMC 3 nm HKMG FinFET (N3-class), INT8 SRAM-based digital CIM macro/compiler test chip
modern.title: A 3 nm FinFET 125 TOPS/W-29 TFLOPS/W, 90 TOPS/mm2-17 TFLOPS/mm2 SRAM-Based INT8, and FP16 Digital-CIM Compiler With Support for Multi-Weight Update/Cycle (Mori et al., IEEE JSSC 61, 1502-1512; earlier version VLSI 2025, DOI 10.23919/VLSITechnologyandCir65189.2025.11074897)
modern.where: abstract (OpenAlex/IEEE abstract text; full paper is closed-access and was not opened)
modern.quote: 124.6 TOPS/W at 0.5 V and 90.2 TOPS/mm2at 1.1 V for INT8 DCIM
modern.conditions: INT8 weights x INT8 activations, digital compute-in-memory MACRO (arithmetic + SRAM weights, no off-macro data movement), measured test chip, 124.6 TOPS/W at 0.5 V (low-voltage best case; 90.2 TOPS/mm2 is at 1.1 V). 1 MAC = 2 ops -> J/MAC = 2/124.6 x 1e-12 = 1.605e-14 J. The abstract states no sparsity or toggle-rate assumption (not stated != none; TSMC's ISSCC 2024 3 nm paper used 25 % input toggle / 50 % weight=1, so a similar convention is possible but unverified).

alternatives.label: highest verified INT8 headline, node nominally 1.8 nm-class, but states 25% input activity
alternatives.title: 30.9 A 147TOPS/W, 250TOPS/mm2, Fully Synthesizable, Digital Compute-in-Memory Accelerator Supporting INT8xINT8 with Zero-Point Quantization in Intel 18A Technology (ISSCC 2026)
alternatives.quote: delivers a peak energy-efficiency of 147TOPS/W at 25% input activity
alternatives.conditions: peak at 0.4 V, 25 C, 25% input activity, 6.1 mW; 1.1 V / 2.62 GHz gives 250 TOPS/mm2; 0.0856 mm2 on-die accelerator, 128 input x 32 output channels (area x density = 21.4 TOPS = 4096 MACs x 2.62 GHz x 2 ops, so 2 ops/MAC); dense (100% activity) figure not given and would be lower.

alternatives.label: possibly better but INT8 NOT verified
alternatives.title: A 2nm 234.4 TOPS/W and 511.9 TOPS/mm2 Digital Computing-in-Memory Compiler with Multiple MAC Units per Weight and Multiple Data Format Support (VLSI 2026)
alternatives.quote: A 2nm 234.4 TOPS/W and 511.9 TOPS/mm2 Digital Computing-in-Memory Compiler
alternatives.conditions: data format/precision, voltage and activity behind the 234.4 TOPS/W figure are not stated in any source opened; do not use unless confirmed as INT8.

alternatives.label: excluded: per-bit-normalised only
alternatives.title: A 4nm 6163-TOPS/W/b 4790-TOPS/mm2/b SRAM Based Digital-Computing-in-Memory Macro (ISSCC 2023)
alternatives.conditions: only a TOPS/W/b figure; INT8 equivalent would need the bit-product normalisation (6163/64 = 96 TOPS/W if normalised by 8x8 bits) which is unverified; not used.

alternatives.label: excluded: INT4 / sparsity / other precision
alternatives.conditions: TSMC 5 nm ISSCC 2022 254 TOPS/W is 4b/4b; NVIDIA 5 nm JSSC 2023 95.6 TOPS/W is 4-bit; TSMC 3 nm ISSCC 2024 32.5 TOPS/W is INT12; IBM 7 nm AI chip 16.9 TOPS/W is INT4; Samsung 5 nm SRAM IMC macro 274 TOPS/W only at 90% input-bit sparsity (precision not stated); Samsung NPUs (ISCA 2021 13.6 TOPS/W, JSSC 2023 4 nm 11.59 TOPS/W) are workload-level numbers.

unresolved: Tan et al. Opt. Lett. 47, 4766 (2022): 0.07 dB/cm is confirmed from the abstract, but the measurement wavelength (1550 nm) is confirmed only via the Skryabin et al. arXiv:2408.06688 citation; the OL full text and the OME 2021 (0.15 dB/cm) full text could not be opened (publisher bot wall). Skryabin's own 0.07 dB/cm and 0.2 dB/facet were measured at 920 nm, not 1550 nm.

No peer-reviewed thin-film LiNbO3 modulator energy per symbol INCLUDING a driver was found; modulator_energy_j uses silicon (microring / MZM) transmitters with integrated drivers. TFLN modulator-only numbers (4.49 fJ/bit driverless, 61-120 fJ/bit estimated from V_rms) are in the notes.

No source isolating the directional-coupler/MZI EXCESS loss (excluding propagation) of fs-written circuits at 1550 nm was opened; loss_per_stage_db is an all-inclusive per-interferometer figure (0.35 dB) that already contains propagation along the MZI. optimistic = nominal for that item.

Heater optimistic (0.72 mW P_2pi) requires a high-vacuum package; the in-air bridge value is 37 mW (mean 18.5 mW). The 17 mW FLICE microbridge result (Photonics 13, 731) was seen only as an abstract (wavelength unverified, full text blocked).

Fibre coupling optimistic (0.2 dB/facet at 1550 nm) is a computed mode-overlap loss (Flamini 2015), not a measured insertion loss; modulator insertion-loss optimistic (< 1 dB) is an upper bound from Kharel et al., which has an Optica erratum (DOI 10.1364/OPTICA.440484) that was not opened. Lower TFLN on-chip loss (e.g. Wang et al. Nature 2018) not verified.
static_power_w: the 12 mW datasheet 'typical' holds only with no heat lift; the 1.2 W measured value belongs to a driver-populated 16-channel module. No measured TEC power for a passive chip found.

Laser optimistic values (50 % WPE, 4.9 W) are multimode broad-area chips; single-mode alternatives (28.5-30 % WPE, 2-3 W) are in the notes. Nominal WPE is derived from datasheet plot readings (+/-10 %). The Thorlabs DFB1550LP and Digi-Key G&H datasheets were read from mirror copies (official thorlabs.com page is JavaScript-only).

Digital modern reference: conditions for TSMC 124.6 TOPS/W (toggle rate/sparsity) are not in the abstract; Intel 18A 147 TOPS/W states 25 % input activity; TSMC 2 nm 234.4 TOPS/W could not be confirmed as INT8. Full papers are closed-access and were not opened.

DAC: the 8-bit DAC values are for 14-28 GS/s research DACs (no 8-bit DAC in the 1-10 GS/s window exists in the Caragiulo-Daigle-Murmann survey, which covers 1996-2020 plus additions); the nominal DAC power (84 mW, Nazemi 2015) comes from the survey, not the paper abstract. ADC values come from the Murmann survey (ISSCC/VLSI only), power numbers match the ISSCC program abstracts.

PD optimistic QE (0.92) is a large-area free-space Ge photodiode, not GHz-class; the high-speed Ge waveguide PD alternative (eta 0.87) was read from the abstract only and its coupling-loss accounting is unverified. TIA optimistic (2 pA/sqrt(Hz)) is a 2.5 GHz, 80 kohm-gain 180 nm CMOS TIA; the IEEE SSC-L letter was read as abstract only.

Horowitz table: values confirmed by viewing the figure image on page 14 of the PDF (the text layer is garbled); the PDF came from a Gwern.net mirror of the IEEE paper, DOI 10.1109/ISSCC.2014.6757323 resolves to the IEEE record.
